akhfash:7-9.t:
He said ﴿فَعَدَلَكَ﴾, that is: thus He created you; and some read it light. Whoever reads it heavy, ﴿عَدَّلَك﴾, is only saying "He proportioned your form" (عَدَّلَ خَلْقَكَ); and "عَدَلَكَ" means: He balanced parts of you against other parts of you and made you even and well-proportioned, and it is in the meaning of "عدّلك".
And He said ﴿خَلَقَكَ﴾ and ﴿رَكَّبَكَ﴾ ﴿كَلاَّ﴾; and if you wish, you say ﴿خَلَقَك﴾ and ﴿رَكَّبَكْ﴾ ﴿كَلاَّ﴾ with assimilation (idghām), because they are two identical letters, and of two identical letters one is assimilated into its companion. And if you wish, when both are vowelled, you make the first quiescent and vowel the second. When the first is quiescent there is no assimilation, and when the first is vowelled and the second quiescent there is no assimilation. «[Translator's note: so in the source; one would expect "when the first is quiescent there is nothing but assimilation".]»

akhfash:19-19.t: And He said ﴿يَوْمَ لاَ تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ﴾: He made "the day" (mean) a time (ḥīn), as if, when He said ﴿وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ﴾, He said "at a time when no soul has power" (في حين لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ). And some read ﴿يَوْمُ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ﴾, making it an explanation of the first "day", as if He said: "it is a day when (no soul) has power" (هُوَ يوم لا تملك).

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَإِذَا الْكَوَاكِبُ انْتَثَرَتْ﴾ break loose and fall,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ فُجِّرَتْ﴾ are opened into one another and become one sea, and the fresh water is mixed with the salt,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَإِذَا الْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ﴾ their earth is overturned and their dead are raised — and the answer (jawāb) of إِذَا and of what is conjoined to it is:

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ﴾ i.e. every soul, at the time of these things mentioned, which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿مَا قَدَّمَتْ﴾ of deeds ﴿وَ﴾ what ﴿أَخَّرَتْ﴾ of them.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ﴾ the unbeliever, ﴿مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ﴾ so that you disobeyed Him,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ﴾ after you were not ﴿فَسَوَّاكَ﴾ made you well-formed, with sound limbs, ﴿فَعَدَلَكَ﴾ without doubling and with doubling: made you balanced in form, with proportionate limbs, no hand or leg longer than the other,

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a deterrent from being deluded by the generosity of Allah the Exalted; ﴿بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾ i.e. the unbelievers of Mecca ﴿بِالدِّينِ﴾ the recompense for deeds,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحَافِظِينَ﴾ of the angels, over your deeds,

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ﴾ the believers who are truthful in their faith ﴿لَفِي نَعِيمٍ﴾ a Garden,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ﴾ the unbelievers ﴿لَفِي جَحِيمٍ﴾ a burning Fire;

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿يَصْلَوْنَهَا﴾ they enter it and suffer its heat ﴿يَوْمَ الدِّينِ﴾ the Recompense,

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَمَا هُمْ عَنْهَا بِغَائِبِينَ﴾ to be taken out.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ﴾ has made you know ﴿مَا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ﴾

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿ثُمَّ مَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ﴾ magnifying its import.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿يَوْمُ﴾ in the nominative, i.e. it is the day [يَوْمَ] ﴿لَا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾ of benefit; ﴿وَالْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ﴾ no one else has any command in it, i.e. He has not enabled anyone to mediate in it, unlike this world.

daas-irab:1-5.t: The i'rab of verses like these has already been given in Sūrat al-Takwīr.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿يا﴾: a vocative particle; ﴿أَيُّهَا﴾: the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; ﴿ها﴾: a particle drawing attention (tanbīh); ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾: badal (substitute); ﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿غَرَّكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of ما; ﴿بِرَبِّكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْكَرِيمِ﴾: naʿt (adjective).

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a second naʿt (adjective) of ربك; ﴿خَلَقَكَ﴾: a past verb and its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿فَسَوَّاكَ﴾: conjoined to خلقك; ﴿فَعَدَلَكَ﴾: also conjoined.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿فِي أَيِّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ركبك; ﴿صُورَةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿ما﴾: redundant (zāʾida); ﴿شاءَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of صورة; ﴿رَكَّبَكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿بَلْ﴾: a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī); ﴿تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بِالدِّينِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and inna is a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters); ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿لَحافِظِينَ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿حافظين﴾ is the postponed noun of inna; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿ما﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿تَفْعَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْأَبْرارَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿لَفِي﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿في نَعِيمٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:14-14.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿يَصْلَوْنَها﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿يَوْمَ الدِّينِ﴾: an adverb of time, muḍāf to الدين.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and ﴿ما﴾ is Ḥijāzī, working like laysa; ﴿هُمْ﴾: its noun; ﴿عَنْها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows; ﴿بِغائِبِينَ﴾: genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of ما; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle and ﴿ما﴾ is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَدْراكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of ما, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿ما يَوْمُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿الدِّينِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause stands in place of the second object of أدراك.

daas-irab:18-18.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is the same.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb; ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿لِنَفْسٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿شَيْئاً﴾: direct object; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَالْأَمْرُ﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle and ﴿الْأَمْرُ﴾ is mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time annexed to one like it, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾: attached to the omitted khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive.

dervis-irab:1-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بُعْثِرَتْ) Al-Zamakhsharī said: "بعثر and بحثر have one meaning; they are composed of البعث (raising) and البحث (searching) with a rāʾ joined to them. The meaning is: they were searched through and their dead brought out. [Sūrat] Barāʾa was called al-Mubaʿthira because it turned out (بعثرت) the secrets of the hypocrites." In al-Mukhtār: "بحثره فتبحثر, i.e. he scattered it and it was scattered. Al-Farrāʾ said: بحثر متاعه وبعثره, i.e. he dispersed it and turned some of it over onto other parts. Abū al-Jarrāḥ said: بحثر الشيء وبعثره, i.e. he extracted it and uncovered it."

* I'rab:
(إِذَا السَّماءُ انْفَطَرَتْ وَإِذَا الْكَواكِبُ انْتَثَرَتْ وَإِذَا الْبِحارُ فُجِّرَتْ وَإِذَا الْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ، عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ) (إذا) is an adverb for future time, putting its protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) in the genitive and itself accusative by its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (السماء) is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb indicated by the one mentioned, and the clause (انفطرت) is explicative. The clause "انفطرت السماء" is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, and the adverb is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the apodosis, which is (علمت). What follows is conjoined to it. (البحار) and (القبور) are the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb. The clause (علمت) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (علمت نفس) is a verb and its fāʿil, (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause (أخّرت) [Translator's note: so in the source; it is (قدّمت) that is the ṣila, with (أخّرت) conjoined to it] has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما).
(يا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسانُ ما غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ) (يا) is a vocative particle; (أيّها) is the one addressed, an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of the accusative by (يا); the hāʾ is for drawing attention; and (الإنسان) is a badal (substitute). (ما) is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (غرّك) is its khabar (predicate). (بربك) is attached to (غرّك), and (الكريم) is an adjective of (ربك). Ibn Jubayr and al-Aʿmash read ما أغرّك, so it may be that أن [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably ما] is interrogative, or that it is of wonder (taʿajjub). He, glory be to Him, said الكريم rather than any other of His beautiful names and attributes only because it is as though He, the Exalted, prompted him with the answer, so that he would say: "The generosity of the Generous deluded me."
(الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ) (الذي) is a second adjective of (ربك), affirming the lordship; the clause (خلقك) is the ṣila of (الذي); (فسوّاك) is conjoined to (خلقك), and likewise (فعدلك).
(فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ ما شاءَ رَكَّبَكَ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (ركبك); (ما) is redundant (zāʾida); the clause (شاء) is an adjective of (صورة), and the mafʿūl bihi is omitted, i.e. شاءها (He willed it). The meaning is: He gave you a description in whatever form His will required, of beauty and ugliness, tallness and shortness, maleness and femaleness. (وعدلك) means: He made you of balanced stature, proportionate in form, without disparity. It may also be attached to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. He assembled you while you are found in one of the forms. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be attached to (عدلك), with (أيّ) having the meaning of wonder, i.e. He balanced you in a wondrous form."
(كَلَّا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِ) (كلا) is a particle of rebuke and restraint, and (بل) is a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī) to the explanation of the real cause of their delusion. Al-Rāghib's wording: "بل here is for validating the second and cancelling the first, as though it were said: there is nothing here that requires anything to delude them regarding Him, the Exalted; rather, it is their denial that drove them to what they committed." (تكذبون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative and its fāʿil, and (بالدين) is attached to (تكذبون).
(وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحافِظِينَ كِراماً كاتِبِينَ) The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), confirming the disapproval, and the clause is a ḥāl from the wāw in (تكذبون), i.e. you deny while the scribes write everything that comes from you. The wāw may also be resumptive, the clause being resumptive, set out to inform them of that so that they may desist from what they are upon. (إنّ) is a particle resembling the verb; (عليكم) is its fronted khabar; the lām is for emphasis; and (حافظين) is the noun of (إنّ), or it is an adjective of its noun, i.e. angels. (كراما) is a naʿt (adjective) of (حافظين), and (كاتبين) a second naʿt.
(يَعْلَمُونَ ما تَفْعَلُونَ) The clause is a third naʿt. (يعلمون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative and the wāw is its fāʿil; (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi; and the clause (تفعلون) is the ṣila, with the referring pronoun omitted, i.e. تفعلونه.
(إِنَّ الْأَبْرارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ لَفِي جَحِيمٍ) The clause is resumptive, set out to answer an implied question, its implied form being "Why do they write that?" — as though it were said: so that He may recompense the righteous with bliss and the wicked with the Blaze. (إنّ) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and (في نعيم) is its khabar. The clause (وإن الفجّار …) is conjoined to the preceding clause and parsed like it.
(يَصْلَوْنَها يَوْمَ الدِّينِ) The clause is a ḥāl from the pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun, namely (لفي جحيم). (يصلونها) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw is its fāʿil, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; (يوم الدين) is an adverb attached to (يصلونها). The clause (يصلونها) may also be resumptive, set out to answer an implied question, its implied form being "And what will their affair come to in the Blaze?"
(وَما هُمْ عَنْها بِغائِبِينَ) He meant: they will roast in the Fire on the Day of Judgement, and they are not absent from it before that, i.e. in their graves.
(وَما أَدْراكَ ما يَوْمُ الدِّينِ ثُمَّ ما أَدْراكَ ما يَوْمُ الدِّينِ) The wāw is a conjunction. (ما) is an interrogative noun of disapproval, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (أدراك) is the khabar. (أدراك) is an imperfect verb [Translator's note: so in the source; أدراك is a past verb] with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, its implied form being "huwa", and the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi. (ما) is an interrogative noun whose meaning is to make terrible and great, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and (يوم الدين) is its khabar. The clause, suspended (muʿallaqa) by the interrogative, stands in place of the second object of (أدراك). Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Everything in the Quran with His saying ما أدراك, He has informed him of it; and everything in it with His saying وما يدريك, He has withheld it from him."
(يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئاً وَالْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ) (يوم) is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember). Abū al-Baqāʾ made it an adverb attached to something omitted, its implied form being "they will be recompensed". It was also read in the nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ or as a badal from (يوم الدين). The clause (لا تملك) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; (نفس) is the fāʿil, its tanwīn being for generalization, i.e. every soul; and (شيئا) is a mafʿūl bihi. (الأمر) is a mubtadaʾ; (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to something omitted as a ḥāl, the tanwīn being a substitute for a clause; and (لله) is the khabar of (الأمر).

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «إن الأبرار لفي نعيم وإن الفجّار لفي جحيم» there is al-waṣl (conjoining). The discussion of waṣl and faṣl (conjoining and disjoining) has preceded. Among the requirements of waṣl present here is the agreement of the two clauses in being declarative or performative (khabariyya / inshāʾiyya), together with a connection, i.e. a common factor between them, which here is contrast.
2- In these two verses there is also the device of al-tarṣīʿ [Translator's note: the source prints الترجيع; the definition given is that of al-tarṣīʿ], a kind of rhymed prose (sajʿ): every word in the first half of the verse or the prose clause corresponds to its counterpart in metre, rhyme-letter and case-ending. Among what has come of it in poetry is the saying of Abū Firās:
وأفعالنا للراغبين كريمة ... وأموالنا للطالبين نهاب
(Our deeds towards those who seek us are generous, and our wealth is booty for those who ask.)

farraa:1-1.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ ٱنفَطَرَتْ﴾: it was split.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ﴾.
What is in its belly of gold and silver came out, and the dead came out after that. It is one of the portents of the Hour that the earth brings out the pieces of its liver (أفلاذ كبدها), of its gold and its silver. Al-Farrāʾ said: الأفلاذ are pieces of liver cut lengthwise, المشرّح and المشرّحة; the singular is فِلْذ and فِلْذة.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ﴾ of its deeds ﴿وَأَخَّرَتْ﴾.
And what it left behind: whatever practice (sunna), good or evil, it established which was then acted upon.
The response (jawāb) to ﴿إذا السَّماء انفطَرتْ﴾ (1) is His saying: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ﴾.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read it: "فَعَدَلَك", lightened, and the people of the Hijaz read it: "فعدَّلك", with shadda. Whoever reads it lightened, its interpretation — and Allah knows best — is: He turned you into whatever form He willed: either handsome or ugly, or tall or short.
He said: [al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying]: One of the shaykhs narrated to me from Layth from Ibn Abī Najīḥ that he said: in the form of a paternal uncle, in the form of a father, in the form of one of the relatives, by resemblance.
Whoever reads "فعدَّلك" with shadda means — and Allah knows best —: He made you well-proportioned, of balanced make. That is the more pleasing of the two to me and the better of them in Arabic, because you say: ﴿فى أى صورة ما شاء ركبك﴾ (in whatever form He willed He assembled you), so making في belong to the assembling (التركيب) is stronger in Arabic than making في belong to العدل (turning); [130/b] because saying عدلتك إلى كذا وكذا (I turned you to such and such) and صرفتك إلى كذا وكذا is better than saying عدلتك فيه and صرفتك فيه.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كَلاَّ بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِٱلدِّينِ﴾.
With tāʾ. Some of the people of Medina read it with yāʾ, and some of them with tāʾ; al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim with tāʾ. The tāʾ is the better of the two because of His saying: "وإِنَّ عَلَيكُم" — He did not say: عليهم.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَا هُمْ عَنْهَا بِغَآئِبِينَ﴾.
He says: once they enter it, they will not be brought out of it. The readers agreed on the accusative in ﴿يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ﴾ (19), and the nominative would be permissible if it were read so. Al-Kisāʾī claimed that the Arabs prefer the nominative when they annex اليوم to يفعل, تفعل, أفعل and نفعل, saying: هذا يومُ نفعلُ ذاك (this is the day we do that), and أفعل ذاك, and نفعل ذاك. But when they say هذا يومَ فعلتَ, annexing يوم to فعلتُ or to إذ, they prefer the accusative. They recited to us:
عَلى حينَ عاتبْتُ المشيبَ على الصِّبا * وقُلتُ أَلَمَّا تَصْحُ والشَّيبُ وازِعُ؟
(At the time when I reproached grey hair for [the loss of] youth, and said: Have you not yet sobered up, when grey hair is a restrainer?)
With the yāʾ and tāʾ [forms] what is permissible with فعلت is also permissible; but most common is what al-Kisāʾī explained.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «علمت» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «الإنسان» is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); the clause «ما غرَّك» is the answer to the vocative, resumptive; «ما»: interrogative, mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause «غرَّك» is the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The preposition «في أيِّ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ركَّبك»; أي: an interrogative noun, genitive (majrūr), declinable; «ما»: redundant (zāʾida); the clause «شاء» is a naʿt (adjective), the link being implied (muqaddar), i.e.: شاءها (He willed it); and the clause «ركبك» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: (كلا بل تكذبون بالدين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: (وإن عليكم لحافظين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) in {تُكَذِّبُونَ}; the lām is for emphasis.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «كراما» is a naʿt (adjective), and «وكاتبين» is a second naʿt.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «يعلمون» is a third naʿt (adjective) of {لَحَافِظِينَ}.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «يصلونها» is a naʿt (adjective) of جحيم, and «يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: (وما هم عنها بغائبين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما»; the preposition «عنها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بغائبين».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The wāw is resumptive, and the clause «ما يوم الدين» is the second object of «أدراك»; «يوم»: khabar (predicate) of the interrogative «ما».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «ثم ما أدراك» is conjoined to the preceding resumptive clause.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: «يوم»: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being (يُجَازَوْن) (they will be recompensed); the clause «والأمر يومئذ لله» is conjoined to the clause «لا تملك»; «يومئذ» is attached to the "being" (istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached; the preposition «لله» is attached to the khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «السماء»: fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it, and the clause «انفطرت» is explicative.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying, the Exalted: (ما غرك): (ما) is an interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (غرك) is the khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying (وما أدراك ما يوم الدين): the discussion of it and of its parallel has already preceded in al-Ḥāqqa, al-Wāqiʿa and elsewhere.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t: His saying (يوم لا تملك نفس لنفس شيئا): whoever reads (يوم) with fatḥa makes it in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the (يوم) before it, or in the position of the accusative as an adverbial, or as a badal from the first (يوم الدين). It is indeclinable (mabnī) according to the Kufans because it is annexed to the verb, and declinable according to the Basrans, accusative as a badal from the first (يوم); and its accusative as an adverbial of the recompense, which is (الدين), is permissible. It is not indeclinable according to them only because it is annexed to a declinable word; it is made indeclinable only when annexed to an indeclinable one, like (يومئذ). Whoever reads it in the nominative makes it a badal from the (يوم الدين) before it, and it may be put in the nominative with an implied (هو).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb for future time, governing its protasis in the genitive and put in the accusative by its apodosis, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿علمت نفس﴾.
﴿السماء﴾: fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb indicated by the one mentioned, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma. The clause made of the omitted verb and the fāʿil is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it.
﴿انفطرت﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, its implied form being "hiya", and the tāʾ is for the feminine. The clause ﴿انفطرت﴾ is explicative, with no grammatical position. The adverb is attached to the apodosis (jawāb), which is ﴿عَلِمَتْ﴾.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and idhā is an adverb for future time, governing its protasis in the genitive and put in the accusative by its apodosis.
﴿الكواكب﴾: fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned after it; the fāʿil is nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma. The clause made of the omitted verb and the fāʿil is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it.
﴿انتثرت﴾: intathara is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, its implied form being "hiya", and the tāʾ is for the feminine. The clause intatharat is explicative, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and idhā is an adverb for future time, governing its protasis in the genitive and put in the accusative by its apodosis.
﴿البحار﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned after it. The clause made of the omitted verb and the nāʾib fāʿil is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it.
﴿فجرت﴾: fujjira is a passive past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with a latent (mustatir) nāʾib fāʿil, its implied form being "hiya", and the tāʾ is for the feminine. The clause ﴿فجرت﴾ is explicative, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and idhā is an adverb for future time, governing its protasis in the genitive and put in the accusative by its apodosis.
﴿القبور﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned after it; the nāʾib fāʿil is nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma. The clause made of the omitted verb and the nāʾib fāʿil is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it.
﴿بعثرت﴾: a passive past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with a latent (mustatir) nāʾib fāʿil, its implied form being "hiya", and the tāʾ is for the feminine. The clause ﴿بعثرت﴾ is explicative, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿علمت﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the tāʾ is for the feminine.
﴿نفس﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿قدمت﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the tāʾ is for the feminine, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "hiya".
﴿و﴾: the wāw is a conjunction.
﴿أخرت﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the tāʾ is for the feminine, and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "hiya". The clause ﴿علمت نفس﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; the clause ﴿قدمت﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿أخرت﴾ is conjoined to ﴿قدمت﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿يا﴾: a vocative particle.
﴿أيها﴾: the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative; hā is for drawing attention (tanbīh).
﴿الإنسان﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾.
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿غرك﴾: gharra is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), its implied form being "huwa", and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿بربك﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and the word ﴿رب﴾ is a genitive noun by the kasra; the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿غرك﴾.
﴿الكريم﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ربك﴾, genitive. The clause ﴿يا أيها...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿ما غرك﴾ is the answer to the vocative, with no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿غرك﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of ﴿ما﴾.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive as a second naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ربك﴾.
﴿خلقك﴾: ﴿خلق﴾ is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the fāʿil (agent) is a pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فسواك﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and sawwāka is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the fāʿil is a pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi.
﴿فعدلك﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and ʿadalaka is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the fāʿil is a pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. The clause ﴿خلقك﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿الذي﴾, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿سواك﴾ is conjoined to ﴿خلقك﴾, with no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿عدلك﴾ is conjoined to ﴿سواك﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿في﴾: a preposition.
﴿أي﴾: a noun in the genitive by the preposition ﴿في﴾, the sign of the genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ركبك﴾.
﴿صورة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿ما﴾: connective (ṣila).
﴿شاء﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the fāʿil (agent) is a pronoun, its implied form being "huwa".
﴿ركبك﴾: rakkaba is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the fāʿil is a pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause ﴿شاء﴾ is in the position of the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿صورة﴾, and the clause ﴿ركبك﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of khalaqaka, sawwāka and ʿadalaka.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿بل﴾: a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī).
﴿تكذبون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿بالدين﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and al-dīn is a genitive noun by the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تكذبون﴾. The clause ﴿تكذبون...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿و﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
﴿إن﴾: a particle of emphasis and accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿عليكم﴾: ʿalā is a preposition and ﴿كم﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿لحافظين﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis, indeclinable on the fatḥa, and ḥāfiẓīn is the postponed noun (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. The clause ﴿إن عليكم لحافظين﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of tukadhdhibūn; or the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿كراما﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حافظين﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿كاتبين﴾: a second naʿt, accusative by the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿يعلمون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿تفعلون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil. The clause ﴿يعلمون﴾ is in the position of the accusative as another naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حافظين﴾, and the clause ﴿تفعلون﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿إن﴾: a particle of emphasis and accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿الأبرار﴾: the noun (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿لفي﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis, and fī is a preposition.
﴿نعيم﴾: a noun in the genitive by the preposition ﴿في﴾, the sign of the genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna. The clause ﴿إن الأبرار لفي نعيم﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿وإن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and inna is a particle of emphasis and accusative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿الفجار﴾: the noun (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿لفي﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) for emphasis, and fī is a preposition.
﴿جحيم﴾: a noun in the genitive by the preposition ﴿في﴾, the sign of the genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna. The clause ﴿إن الفجار لفي جحيم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿إن الأبرار لفي نعيم﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿يصلونها﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent), and ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿يوم﴾: an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿الدين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the kasra. The clause ﴿يصلونها﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in the implied khabar (predicate) of inna; it is also said to be in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿جحيم﴾. Yawm is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يصلونها﴾.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿و﴾: the wāw is a conjunction.
﴿ما﴾: a negative particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn that works like laysa.
﴿هم﴾: a detached pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of ﴿ما﴾.
﴿عنها﴾: ʿan is a preposition, and ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿غائبين﴾.
﴿بغائبين﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ghāʾibīn is a noun genitive in form by the yāʾ and accusative by position as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿ما﴾. The clause ﴿ما هم بغائبين﴾ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in ﴿يصلونها﴾.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿و﴾: the wāw is resumptive.
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أدراك﴾: a past verb indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿يوم﴾: khabar (predicate) of ﴿ما﴾, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿الدين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the kasra. The clause ﴿ما أدراك﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿أدراك﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the first ﴿ما﴾; and the interrogative clause ﴿ما يوم الدين﴾ is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the second and third objects of the verb ﴿أدراك﴾, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction.
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أدراك﴾: a past verb indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿يوم﴾: khabar (predicate) of ﴿ما﴾, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿الدين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the kasra. The interrogative clause ﴿ما يوم الدين﴾ is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the second and third objects of the verb ﴿أدراك﴾, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative; and the second clause ﴿ما أدراك﴾ is conjoined to the first clause ﴿ما أدراك﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿يوم﴾: an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "yujāzūn" (they will be requited) or "udhkur" (mention).
﴿لا﴾: a negative particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿تملك﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿نفس﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿لنفس﴾: the lām is a preposition and nafs is a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿تملك﴾.
﴿شيئا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by the fatḥa.
﴿والأمر﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and al-amr is mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿يومئذ﴾: yawm: an adverb of time, accusative by the fatḥa, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of al-amr; idh: a noun indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) sukūn, because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause.
﴿لله﴾: the lām is a preposition, and the Name of Majesty is a noun in the genitive by the lām, the sign of the genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of al-amr. The clause ﴿لا تملك﴾ is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause ﴿الأمر يومئذ لله﴾ is in the position of the accusative of [Translator's note: the source appears to omit the word "ḥāl" here, i.e. "a ḥāl of"] the fāʿil of ﴿تملك﴾, the linking element being implied, i.e. "fīhi" (in it).

nahhas-irab:1-3.t: إِذَا السَّماءُ انْفَطَرَتْ (1): [the verb is feminine] because السماء is feminine in the most eloquent usage; al-Farrāʾ reported the masculine for it. Whoever makes it feminine forms its diminutive as سميّة, even though it is of four letters in origin, because a letter has been dropped from it. السماء is nominative by an implied verb, and likewise وَإِذَا الْكَواكِبُ انْتَثَرَتْ (2), and likewise وَإِذَا الْبِحارُ فُجِّرَتْ (3). It is not permissible that it be nominative by the other [overt] verb, except according to something ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān reported to us from Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā Thaʿlab, who said: [in] زيد قام, [Zayd] is nominative by its verb, which is intended to be placed after it. It was said: the meaning of وَإِذَا الْبِحارُ فُجِّرَتْ (3) is that some of them were made to burst into others, because of the convulsion of the earth with the passing away of the mountains and the earthquakes, so that some seas mingled with others.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: [وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ, in the second person. Translator's note: this entry continues the sentence of the previous one.] Abū Jaʿfar said: I do not know what he reported from some of the people of Medina, and I know of no one besides him who related it.

nahhas-irab:11-12.t: كِراماً كاتِبِينَ (11) is a naʿt (adjective) of حافظين, and likewise يَعْلَمُونَ ما تَفْعَلُونَ (12).

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: إِنَّ الْأَبْرارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ (13): i.e. those who were righteous through obedience to Allah and avoidance of His acts of disobedience. Al-Ḥasan said: الأبرار are those who do not harm [even] the tiny ants.

nahhas-irab:14-15.t: [يَصْلَوْنَها is feminine] on the basis that النار is feminine, even though الجحيم is masculine.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: That is, once they have been made to enter it, they will not come out of it. Qatāda said: [يوم الدين is] the day people are requited for their deeds.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: It was said: this is not a repetition. The meaning is: "And what will make you know what is in the Day of Judgement of punishment and exemplary chastisement for the wicked? Then what will make you know what is in the Day of Judgement of bliss for the righteous?"

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئاً is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. Al-Farrāʾ said «in his book on the meanings» [Maʿānī al-Qurʾān]: the readers agreed on the accusative of «يوم لا تملك». Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake. Abū ʿAmr, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj — who is one of the two teachers of Nāfiʿ — read يَوْمُ لا تَمْلِكُ in the nominative. [Translator's note: the source prints the vowel of the cited reading as fatḥa.] For whoever reads the nominative, the implied form is "it is يَوْمُ لا تَمْلِكُ"; it may also be a badal (substitute) for what precedes it: ثُمَّ ما أَدْراكَ ما يَوْمُ الدِّينِ (18) يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئاً. For whoever reads the accusative, the implied form is "the judgement is on the day when [a soul] does not possess", and like it is وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْقارِعَةُ يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ [al-Qāriʿa: 3, 4], i.e. the Calamity is on the day when people will be. It is also possible that the implied form is "they will burn in it on the Day of Judgement, يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئاً". These are two views, the first being the preferable of them. Al-Farrāʾ has a third view: he permitted «يوم» to be in the position of the nominative, but made indeclinable (mabnī), as the poet said: [al-ṭawīl] 546- على حين عاتبت المشيب على الصّبا (At the time when I reproached grey hair for [the loss of] youth). Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake. According to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, adverbs cannot be made indeclinable together with something declinable, and the imperfect verb is declinable. As for al-Kisāʾī, he permitted that in poetry out of necessity, and the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, is not to be interpreted on the basis of something like this. Rather, adverbs of time are made indeclinable together with the past verb, as in the verse, because adverbs of time are transient, not fixed, so you may make them indeclinable together with what follows them when that is not declinable, or decline them according to their original state, as in the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He: وَمِنْ خِزْيِ يَوْمِئِذٍ [Hūd: 66], declining يوم, or, if you wish, وَمِنْ خِزْيِ يَوْمَئِذٍ. [Translator's note: the source prints both variants as «يَوْمِئِذٍ»; the second, with the indeclinable fatḥa, is supplied from the sense.] On this basis يوم is made indeclinable with «إذ» on the fatḥa in the positions of nominative, genitive and accusative; and likewise وَالْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: He is saying: they were overturned (بحثرت). Al-Farrāʾ interpreted it as the earth being overturned so that it cast out the treasures and the dead in it, and he cited as evidence the ḥadīth «تلقي الأرض أفلاذ كبدها» ("The earth will cast out the pieces of its liver"). Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake. The Quran does not have "and when the earth"; in it is specifically the graves. And «وتلقي أفلاذ كبدها» — there is no disagreement among the people of knowledge that it is at the end of time and not on the Day of Resurrection. [Translator's note: the source has «أفلا كبدها» in its second citation of the ḥadīth, a misprint for «أفلاذ».]

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
[عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ] completes the statement, and it is the answer (jawāb) of «إذا». There are two views on its meaning. Ibn Zayd said: ما قدمت is what it did, and ما أخّرت is what it left, neglected and deferred of what it was commanded to put forward of the command of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He. The other view is that the meaning of ما أخّرت is a practice (sunna) that it established and that was acted upon after it. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is from Ibn ʿAbbās, and it is preferable; the people of ḥadīth hold it, while some of the people of whims (ahl al-ahwāʾ) reject it.
The evidence of its soundness is that when a person neglects what he was commanded and defers it, that is among the evil he has put forward, not among what he has deferred.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: ما is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is a complete noun; the kāf is in the position of the accusative by غرّ.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: [فَعَدَّلَكَ with doubling] is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries, the people of Basra and the people of Syria. The Kufans read فَعَدَلَكَ without doubling. Al-Farrāʾ considered it unlikely, even though it is the reading of his own school, because one only says عدلته إلى كذا ("I turned him to such-and-such") and صرفته إليه, and one hardly says عدّلته في كذا or صرّفته. Abū Jaʿfar said about it: This is a mistake, because the statement is complete at «فعدلك», and «في» is attached to ركّبك, not to عدلك, for it to be as he said. The meaning of عدلك in the language is "He created you well-proportioned", one leg not longer than the other, and likewise the rest of your form. عدّلك may also be an intensive of عدلك, so they would have one meaning, as Ibn al-Zibaʿrā said: [al-ramal] 545- وعدلنا مثل بدر فاعتدل (And we made up the equivalent of Badr, so it was evened out) — i.e. we killed of them as many as they had killed of us. It was also said: عدلك means He inclined you to whatever He willed of beauty and ugliness, health and sickness.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
ما is redundant (zāʾida). Mujāhid said: [i.e.] in the likeness of a father, or a mother, or a paternal uncle, or a maternal uncle.
كَلَّا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِ (9) وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحافِظِينَ (10)

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: Al-Farrāʾ reported from some of the people of Medina «بل يكذبون», and he rejected it because after it is

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {فُجِّرَتْ}: The majority read it in the passive with doubling. Mujāhid read it in the active without doubling, from al-fujūr (transgressing bounds), with regard to His saying {بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ لاَّ يَبْغِيَانِ} [al-Raḥmān: 20]: when the barrier is removed, they transgress. Mujāhid also, al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym, al-Zaʿfarānī and al-Thawrī read it in the passive without doubling.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {بُعْثِرَتْ}: i.e. overturned. One says baʿtharahu and baḥtharahu, with ʿayn and with ḥāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "They are compounded from al-baʿth (raising) and al-baḥth (searching), with a rāʾ joined to them." He means that they are among words whose meanings agree, because the rāʾ is added in them even though it is not one of the augment letters; this is like damith and dimathr, and sabiṭa and sibaṭr. «عَلِمَتْ» is the apodosis (jawāb) of «إذا».

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {مَا غَرَّكَ}: The majority read «غَرَّك» as a triliteral, with «ما» interrogative, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Ibn Jubayr and al-Aʿmash read «ما أَغَرَّك»; it may then be interrogative or exclamatory. The meaning of agharrahu («أغرَّه») is: made him enter into heedlessness (al-ghirra), or made him heedless.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {الذي خَلَقَكَ}: It admits following [the preceding noun] as a badal (substitute), as explication (bayān) or as a naʿt (adjective), and severance (qaṭʿ) to the nominative or the accusative.
His saying: {فَعَدَلَكَ}: The Kufans read «عَدَلَك» without doubling, and the rest / with doubling. The doubled form means: He made you proportionate in your limbs, so He did not make one of your hands or feet longer, nor one of your eyes wider; it is from al-taʿdīl (proportioning). The reading without doubling admits this, i.e. He balanced some of your limbs with others; and it may be from al-ʿudūl (turning), i.e. He turned you to whatever He willed of forms, shapes and likenesses.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {في أَىِّ صُورَةٍ}: Several views are possible concerning it. The first: that it is attached to «رَكَّبَكَ», «ما» being redundant (zāʾida) on this view, and «شاءَ» an adjective of «صورةٍ». He did not conjoin «رَكَّبَكَ» to what precedes it with the fāʾ, as He conjoined what precedes it with it, because it is an explication of His saying «فَعَدَلَكَ». The implied form is: He proportioned you: He assembled you in whatever form He willed of the wondrous, beautiful forms. The meaning is: He placed you in a form that His will required: of beauty and ugliness, tallness and shortness, maleness and femaleness. The second: that it is attached to something omitted as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. He assembled you, being in one of the forms. The third: that it is attached to «عَدَلَكَ»; the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] transmitted this from some interpreters and did not object to it. But it is open to objection, in that «أيّ» contains the meaning of interrogation and so has the head of the sentence; how then can what precedes it govern it?
It is as though al-Zamakhsharī sensed this, for he said: "«أيّ» has the meaning of wonder, i.e. He proportioned you in what a wondrous form!" This cannot well justify the governing word preceding the interrogative noun, even if the meaning of wonder has entered it. Do you not see that «كيف» and «أنَّى», even if the meaning of wonder enters them, do not have their governing word placed before them? The grammarians disagreed concerning the interrogative noun when confirmation (istithbāt) is intended by it: may its governing word precede it or not? The correct view is that it may not. Likewise, the governing word of declarative «كم» may not precede it, because of its resemblance in form to the interrogative; so this is all the more so. On its being attached to «عَدَلَكَ», «ما» is accusative by «شاء», i.e. He assembled you in whatever assembling He willed, i.e. a beautiful assembling; al-Zamakhsharī said this. Its apparent sense is that it is accusative as a maṣdar (absolute object).
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«ما» may be redundant, or it may be conditional; on both, the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «صورة» and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. He assembled you upon it. And «في» is attached to «رَكَّبك». It was also said: the clause has no position, because «في» is attached to one of the two verbs and the whole is one utterance; the interrogative only precedes «ما» because that is its right." His saying "to one of the two verbs" means «شاءَ» and «رَكَّبك». So three aspects result for «ما»: redundancy; being conditional, in which case its apodosis is omitted; and being accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. standing in the place of a maṣdar.

semin-durr:9-9.t: The majority read «يُكَذِّبُون» as address «[Translator's note: so in the text; the address reading is «تُكَذِّبُون»]». Al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read it with the yāʾ of the third person.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ}: The clause may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «تُكَذِّبون», i.e. you deny while this is the situation; or it may be resumptive: He informed them of that so that they would desist.

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {يَعْلَمُونَ}: It may be a naʿt (adjective), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of «كاتبين», or a naʿt of «جحيم», or resumptive.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {يَصْلَوْنَهَا}: It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition-phrase, since it serves as khabar (predicate); or it may be resumptive. The majority read «يَصْلَوْنَها» without doubling, in the active, and Ibn Miqsam with doubling, in the passive. Its like has preceded.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ لاَ تَمْلِكُ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «يوم» in the nominative, as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is the day". Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be a badal (substitute) for what precedes it, meaning His saying «يومَ الدين». Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, read «يومٌ» nominative with tanwīn, cutting it off from the iḍāfa (genitive construct) and making the clause an adjective of it, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "on which [no soul] has power". The rest read «يومَ» with fatḥa. It was said: it is a fatḥa of iʿrāb, and it is accusative by an implied «أعني» or «يتجاوزون», or by an implied «اذكُرْ», so that it is a direct object. According to the view of the Kufans it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ and was only made indeclinable (mabnī) because of its iḍāfa to the verb, even though [the verb] is declinable, like His saying {هذا يَوْمُ يَنفَعُ} [al-Māʾida: 119]; this has preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْفَطَرَتْ (١)).
The apodosis (jawāb) of «إِذَا» is (عَلِمَتْ).

ukberi-tibyan:6-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ (٦) الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ (٧)).
(مَا غَرَّكَ) is an interrogative and nothing else; had it been an exclamation of wonder (taʿajjub), He would have said «مَا أَغَرَّكَ».
(عَدَلَكَ) with doubling (عَدَّلَكَ) means: He made your form upright; and without doubling (عَدَلَكَ) it has this same meaning. It may also mean: He turned you away from a disliked form.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ مَا شَاءَ رَكَّبَكَ (٨)).
The words of the Exalted (مَا شَاءَ): «مَا» may be redundant (zāʾida), or conditional; on both views the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «صُورَةٍ», and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. «رَكَّبَكَ عَلَيْهَا» (He assembled you in it).
(فِي) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «رَكَّبَكَ». It is also said that the clause has no position, because «فِي» is attached to one of the two verbs, so the whole is a single statement; the interrogative was merely placed before what it properly belongs to.

ukberi-tibyan:10-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحَافِظِينَ (١٠) كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ (١١) يَعْلَمُونَ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ (١٢)).
(كِرَامًا) is a naʿt (adjective), and likewise «يَعْلَمُونَ»; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they write knowing.

ukberi-tibyan:14-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ لَفِي جَحِيمٍ (١٤) يَصْلَوْنَهَا يَوْمَ الدِّينِ (١٥)).
The words of the Exalted (يَصْلَوْنَهَا): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the khabar (predicate), or a naʿt (adjective) of «جَحِيمٍ».

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ لَا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا وَالْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ (١٩)).
The words of the Exalted (يَوْمَ لَا تَمْلِكُ): it is read in the nominative, i.e. «هُوَ يَوْمُ» (it is a day); and in the accusative on the implied form «أَعْنِي يَوْمَ…» (I mean the day…). It is also said that the implied form is «يُجَازَوْنَ يَوْمَ» (they will be recompensed on the day), indicated by the mention of «الدِّين» (the Judgement). It is also said that it properly should be nominative,
but it was given a fatḥa according to the rule of the adverb (ẓarf), as in the words of the Exalted (وَمِنْهُمْ دُونَ ذَلِكَ). According to the Kufans it is indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Infiṭār
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إذا السَّماءُ انْفَطَرَتْ﴾, that is: "split open". The heaven will split open on the Day of Resurrection with the clouds, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said.
«[Translator's note: the source quotes no verse after "as He said".]»

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَإذا الكَواكِبُ انْتَثَرَتْ﴾, that is: they fell down and dropped one after another.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَإذا البِحارُ فُجِّرَتْ﴾: the sweet water burst forth into the salt.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿وَإذا القُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ﴾: he means «بُحْثِرَتْ», that is: their earth is turned over and the dead in them are resurrected.

zajjaj:5-5.t: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ وأخَّرَتْ﴾: what it sent ahead of the deeds it was commanded to do, and what it held back of them and did not do. It was also said: «وَأخَّرَتْ» means: whatever practice (sunna) it instituted that was acted upon after it.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الإنْسانُ ما غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الكَرِيمِ﴾, that is: what deceived you and enticed you until you neglected what was obligatory upon you?!

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ﴾, that is: He created you in the best stature. It is read «فَعَدَّلَكَ» both without doubling and with doubling.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿فِي أيِّ صُورَةٍ ما شاءَ رَكَّبَكَ﴾: «ما» may be an emphasising connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant), and the meaning is: "in whatever form He willed He assembled you — whether tall or short, whether handsome or otherwise." And «ما» may be in the sense of condition and requital (sharṭ wa-jazāʾ), so that the meaning is: "in whatever form He wills to assemble you in, He assembles you."

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿كَلا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِ﴾, that is: rather, you deny that you will be resurrected and judged, that is, requited for your deeds. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, informed them that their deeds are preserved, saying: ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ ما تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 12], so they write it down against them.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿يَصْلَوْنَها يَوْمَ الدِّينِ﴾: the Day of Requital, which is the Day of Resurrection.

zajjaj:17-18.t: His saying: ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما يَوْمُ الدِّينِ﴾ ﴿ثُمَّ ما أدْراكَ ما يَوْمُ الدِّينِ﴾: He repeated the mention of the day to magnify its importance.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾ — it was also read «يَوْمُ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ». Whoever read it in the nominative did so on the basis that the "day" is an attribute (ṣifa) of His saying «يَوْمُ الدِّينِ». It may also be nominative with «هُوَ» implied, so that the meaning is: "it is a day when no soul will have power to do anything for another soul." It may also be in the position of the nominative while being indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, because it is annexed to His saying «لا تَمْلِكُ»; for what is annexed to something not fully declinable (ghayr al-mutamakkin) may be made indeclinable on the fatḥa, even though it is in the position of a nominative or a genitive, as the poet said:
؎لَمْ يَمْنَعِ الشُّرْبَ مِنها غَيْرَ أنْ نَطَقَتْ ∗∗∗ حَمامَةٌ في غُصُونٍ ذاتِ أوْقالِ
(Nothing kept her from drinking except that a dove cooed among branches laden with fruit.)
— he annexed «غَيْرَ» to «أنْ نَطَقَتْ» and so made it indeclinable on the fatḥa. And its accusative may be according to the meaning of these things mentioned: it is ﴿يَوْمَ لا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا﴾.
